verdict.line: You lose extended trades if you auto-attack into Counter Strike (E) or eat an Empowered Leap Strike (Q) unpunished, and you win by all-inning the instant both of those are on cooldown.

brief.thesis: Jax's whole kit is built to punish basic attacks: Leap Strike (Q) closes the gap and Counter Strike (E) dodges every auto you throw during its stance, so trading autos into him is how you lose the lane. Riven's damage is mostly ability damage through Runic Blade-charged strikes and Ki Burst (W), which Counter Strike does not dodge, so your trades should be Q-into-AA-into-W, not straight autos. That structural mismatch is why the numbers land almost even overall (49.6% Riven in this lane, 18,895 games) but tilt toward Riven in this specific matchup (53.9% over 399 games) — it's a cooldown-reading matchup, not a stat-check.

theirWindow.when: Empower (W) glow up, Leap Strike ready
theirWindow.what: He can leap in with a bonus-damage empowered hit and follow with Counter Strike bait. Step back or use Valor (E) to block the empowered auto/leap damage instead of trading autos into it.

yourWindow.when: his Leap Strike and Counter Strike both down
yourWindow.what: All-in immediately with Ki Burst (W) to stun, then dump Broken Wings (Q) charges and autos for the full Runic Blade combo — he has no dodge and no gap-closer to escape or reset the fight.

powerCurve.note: Leap Strike (700 range) threatens before your Ki Burst is up
Ki Burst stun plus Valor dash wins short trades
his Relentless Assault (R) offsets your Wind Slash threat
Eclipse/Axiom Arc spikes win all-in burst windows
Equipment Mastery bonus health stabilizes his HP pool

start.why: Wins the run of short trades in levels 1-2 and sustains through Leap Strike pokes while you wait for Ki Burst at level 3 (54.8% win rate, 91.9% pick over 456 games).

boots.why: The lower cooldowns on Q/W/E let you re-enter the Broken Wings/Ki Burst combo faster during his Counter Strike downtime (57.8% win rate, 56.6% pick over 270 games).

core.why: The proc'd shield covers the empowered auto he lands off Empower (W), and the burst spike matches your all-in windows when his E is down (63.6% win rate as a path start, 33 games).
Bleed-and-heal keeps you alive through his extended Relentless Assault (R) trades once he hits 6 (present in the two highest-winrate paths, 59.1% and 63.6%).
Sustained damage and healing off ability hits reinforces the ability-damage trade pattern Counter Strike can't dodge (in all three top build paths).

situational.when: you are ahead and want faster Q/E resets to chain all-ins before his cooldowns reset (73.7% win rate, 12.3% pick as a path start)
he starts stacking bonus health off Equipment Mastery and you need armor shred to keep burst relevant
he is snowballing off empowered autos and Relentless Assault stacks and you need the flat physical reduction instead (45% win rate, 22.9% pick)

runes.keystoneWhy: The stacking adaptive damage and healing rewards exactly the extended ability-trade pattern this matchup calls for, since you're landing Q/W hits rather than autos into his E.

summoners.why: Ignite punishes his Equipment Mastery-inflated health pool and closes out all-in windows once Leap Strike and Counter Strike are both down (55.1% win rate, 94.9% pick).

playing.title: Never auto into Counter Strike
playing.detail: The moment he activates E he dodges all incoming basic attacks. If he pops it mid-trade, stop auto-attacking and either disengage or keep hitting him with Q/W ability damage, which isn't dodged.

playing.title: Track the Empower glow
playing.detail: Empower (W, 7/6/5/4/3s cooldown) buffs his next auto or Leap Strike. If you see the glow up while he's near your dash range, expect a bonus-damage leap-in and hold Valor (E) to block it.

playing.title: Punish long Leap Strike cooldowns early
playing.detail: Leap Strike is 17s at rank 1, only dropping to 5s by rank 5. If he misses or uses it to reposition before level 5, that's a 10+ second window with no gap-closer — walk up and all-in.

playing.title: Stack Runic Blade before committing Q
playing.detail: Auto-attack once or twice to charge Runic Blade before dumping Broken Wings (Q) charges, so each reactivation hits harder instead of trading raw ability damage alone.

playing.title: Save Wind Slash for the execute
playing.detail: Once Blade of the Exile (R) is up at level 6, hold the Wind Slash charge for when he's already low from a Ki Burst (W) trade rather than opening with it.

playing.title: Use Valor to answer his engage, not just to poke
playing.detail: Valor (E) blocks incoming damage during the dash. Save at least one charge to eat the Empowered Leap Strike hit instead of burning it purely for extra Runic Blade stacks.

playing.title: Play for short trades before level 6
playing.detail: Relentless Assault (R) has no cooldown and only comes online at 6, so before that his sustained-attack scaling isn't active — favor quick in-and-out trades over standing in extended auto exchanges.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and win rates above are pulled from measured OP.GG games on the current patch (16.18.1); the cooldown reads, trade sequencing, and power-curve calls are my own tactical judgment layered on top.

stats.opponentTip: Retreat with your abilities when Jax tries to close in with his Leap Strike (Q) – Counter Strike (E) combo. Harass Jax with your abilities, but keep an eye out for his (P) and Conqueror’s stacks.
